scenes.title: Slaves in Egypt
beats: Long ago, God’s people, the Israelites, lived in Egypt. There were so many of them that the new king, Pharaoh, grew afraid.
So Pharaoh made them his slaves. They had to work hard all day long, making bricks out of mud and straw under the hot sun.

layers.prompt: A hot afternoon in ancient Egypt: tired Israelite slaves in simple robes shape mud bricks and carry them in baskets toward a half-built temple, right of center, while a stern Egyptian taskmaster watches; palm trees and the river Nile in the distance

scenes.title: A Baby in a Basket
beats: One Israelite mother had a baby boy. To keep him safe from Pharaoh, she hid him for three whole months.
When he got too big to hide, she made a little basket, covered it with tar so it would float, and laid him among the reeds by the river Nile. His big sister Miriam stayed to watch.

layers.prompt: At dawn among tall reeds at the edge of the river Nile: a mother gently sets a little woven basket with her baby inside onto the water, right of center, as a young girl, Miriam, watches from behind the reeds

scenes.title: The Princess Finds Him
beats: Pharaoh’s daughter came down to the river to bathe. She saw the basket, opened it — and there was the baby, crying! She felt sorry for him.
Miriam ran up. “Shall I find someone to feed the baby for you?” And she brought the baby’s own mother!
When the boy grew older, the princess adopted him as her son, and she named him Moses.

layers.prompt: Tall green reeds along the river Nile in morning light: a little woven basket with a baby inside floats among the reeds, right of center, as an Egyptian princess in white linen with her maids kneels at the water's edge to lift it out, while a young girl, Miriam, peeks out from the reeds

edits: Remove the second basket floating in the reeds on the right, so only the basket the princess is holding remains; the reeds and water fill that spot.

scenes.title: Moses Runs Away
beats: Moses grew up in Pharaoh’s palace. But one day he saw an Egyptian beating one of his own people, and Moses got so angry that he did something terrible.
Pharaoh was furious, so Moses ran far away into the desert.
There, by a well, he helped some young shepherd girls water their sheep. He married one of them, Zipporah, and became a shepherd himself.

layers.prompt: A stone well in the wide desert of Midian at sunset: Moses, a young man, helps seven shepherd girls draw water for their thirsty sheep and goats, right of center

questions: How do you think Miriam felt, watching her baby brother float down the river?
God kept baby Moses safe. When have you felt safe and cared for?
Who are the people God has given to look after you?

verse.text: God saw the Israelites and took notice.
